name: Miramar
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Miramar, FL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Miramar, FL: two city tree lightings, the Fiesta Navidena at Shirley Branca Park and The Nutcracker at Miramar Cultural Center.
lede: Miramar celebrates in two places: two city tree lightings at Town Center and Shirley Branca Park, a Latin Christmas fiesta and a Nutcracker at the Miramar Cultural Center.
celebrates: The City of Miramar Parks and Recreation lights the season on two nights, with a Holiday Tree Lighting at City Hall in the Town Center and Miramar's Very Merry Celebration at Shirley Branca Park, where winter snow and a special visitor from the North Pole join live entertainment. The same park hosts Fiesta Navidena, hosted by the vice mayor, with Latin music, cultural displays of holiday traditions, a children's fun zone with Santa photos and a toy drive. The Miramar Cultural Center adds The Nutcracker by Ballet Etudes.
lastyear: The City of Miramar's own pages show how it plans each season: a two-night Holiday Tree Lighting, one at City Hall at 2300 Civic Center Place and one at Shirley Branca Park, 6900 Miramar Parkway, both free and open to everyone. The city asks families to bring their own chairs and blankets to the Shirley Branca Park night, which adds winter snow and a special visitor from the North Pole.
facts: Miramar was incorporated on May 26, 1955, with fewer than 200 people. Its first mayor, Robert Gordon, gave the city its name: Miramar means Look at the Sea in Spanish, after an exclusive suburb of Havana. The city seal carries the motto Beauty and Progress. A.L. Mailman founded the city as a bedroom community for Miami and Fort Lauderdale and built 56 inexpensive homes on land bought in 1953.
trains: Miramar does not have its own train station. Tri-Rail's Hollywood stops are Sheridan Street Station at 2900 Sheridan Street and Hollywood Station at 3001 Hollywood Boulevard. Tri-Rail also reaches Metrorail Transfer and MiamiCentral in Miami. For a train day, the Gold Coast Railroad Museum in Miami has the presidential car Ferdinand Magellan and a narrow gauge train ride.
train_links: More than 40 historic rail cars, the presidential car Ferdinand Magellan and a narrow gauge train ride in Miami.
traditions: Holiday Tree Lighting at City Hall
A free evening in the Town Center at 2300 Civic Center Place to light the city's tree.
A second free tree lighting at Shirley Branca Park with live entertainment, winter snow and a visitor from the North Pole.
A Latin Christmas night at Shirley Branca Park with salsa, merengue, Santa photos and a toy drive.
The Nutcracker at the Cultural Center
Ballet Etudes of South Florida dances the Nutcracker at Miramar Cultural Center.
kidfact: Miramar is named after a place in Cuba, and the word means Look at the Sea.
faq: Where is the Miramar tree lighting?

The City of Miramar holds two free tree lightings: one at Miramar City Hall, 2300 Civic Center Place, and one at Shirley Branca Park, 6900 Miramar Parkway. Both run from 6:30 to 8:30 pm, and the city says the community celebrations are open to everyone.
Is there snow at a Miramar holiday event?

The city lists winter snow at Miramar's Very Merry Celebration at Shirley Branca Park, together with live entertainment, a tree lighting and a special visitor from the North Pole. Bring your own chairs and blankets.
Can kids see Santa in Miramar?

Yes. Fiesta Navidena at Shirley Branca Park lists Santa photos in its children's fun zone, and the city's Very Merry Celebration lists a special visitor from the North Pole. Check each host's page for this year's date.
How did Miramar get its name?
The city's history says its first mayor, Robert Gordon, named it. Miramar means Look at the Sea in Spanish, after an exclusive suburb of Havana. The city was incorporated on May 26, 1955.
Which train stations are near Miramar?
Miramar has no station of its own. Tri-Rail's Hollywood stops are Sheridan Street Station at 2900 Sheridan Street and Hollywood Station at 3001 Hollywood Boulevard.
